tracks.title: Pachelbel — Canon in D
tracks.intro_text: Next... from Johann Pachelbel, the Canon in D major, in an arrangement by Frank Hudson. Pachelbel was a German organist and composer of the seventeenth century, and he taught Johann Christoph Bach, the elder brother of Johann Sebastian. Here is the Canon, played by the Strolling Strings of the United States Air Force Band.

tracks.title: Bach — Air (Orchestral Suite No. 3)
tracks.intro_text: From Johann Sebastian Bach... the Air, from the Orchestral Suite number 3 in D major, B.W.V. 1068. In the nineteenth century, a violinist's arrangement made it famous as the Air on the G String, and the name stayed. Performed now by the Air Force Strings, of the United States Air Force Band.

tracks.title: Bach — Largo, Keyboard Concerto in F minor, BWV 1056
tracks.intro_text: Now, a slow movement by Johann Sebastian Bach... the Largo, from the Keyboard Concerto number 5 in F minor, B.W.V. 1056. Bach also used this gentle melody as the opening sinfonia of one of his cantatas. Michel Rondeau is at the harpsichord.

tracks.title: Corelli — Christmas Concerto, Pastorale
tracks.intro_text: From Arcangelo Corelli... the Pastorale, from the Concerto Grosso in G minor, opus 6, number 8, known as the Christmas Concerto. Corelli was an Italian violinist and composer, and his twelve concerti grossi were published in 1714, the year after his death. Performed by the Advent Chamber Orchestra.

tracks.title: Vivaldi — Largo, Concerto in D, RV 93
tracks.intro_text: Antonio Vivaldi now... the Largo, from the Concerto in D major, R.V. 93, written for lute, two violins, and continuo. Tonight it comes to us in an arrangement for accordion orchestra, by Paul De Bra.

tracks.title: Albinoni — Adagio, Oboe Concerto in D minor, Op. 9 No. 2
tracks.intro_text: From Tomaso Albinoni... the Adagio, from the Oboe Concerto in D minor, opus 9, number 2. Albinoni was a Venetian composer of the Baroque, and among the first Italians to write concertos for the oboe. The soloist is Paul Arden-Taylor.

tracks.title: Bach — Sinfonia, Christmas Oratorio
tracks.performer: Phiroz Dalal, St Matthew's Concert Choir and Orchestra
tracks.intro_text: Johann Sebastian Bach... the Sinfonia that opens Part Two of the Christmas Oratorio, B.W.V. 248, a gentle pastoral piece for the shepherds in the fields. Bach first performed the oratorio in Leipzig in the winter of 1734. Phiroz Dalal conducts the St Matthew's Concert Choir and Orchestra.

tracks.title: Handel — Pastoral Symphony (Pifa), Messiah
tracks.performer: MIT Concert Choir & Orchestra, W. Cutter
tracks.intro_text: From George Frideric Handel... the Pastoral Symphony from Messiah... the movement Handel called the Pifa. Handel wrote Messiah in 1741, and it was first heard in Dublin the following spring. From a performance by the M.I.T. Concert Choir and orchestra.

tracks.title: Satie — Gymnopédie No. 1
tracks.intro_text: Erik Satie now... the first Gymnopédie, marked slow and sorrowful. Satie was a French composer and pianist, and he wrote his three Gymnopédies in 1888. Robin Alciatore is the pianist.

tracks.title: Mozart — Adagio, Clarinet Concerto in A, K. 622
tracks.performer: William McColl, basset clarinet; University of Washington Symphony, Abraham Kaplan
tracks.intro_text: From Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart... the Adagio from the Clarinet Concerto in A major, K. 622. Mozart wrote it in 1791 for his friend, the clarinetist Anton Stadler... it is one of the last works he completed. William McColl is the soloist, on a basset clarinet of his own construction, with the University of Washington Symphony Orchestra, conducted by Abraham Kaplan.

tracks.title: Ravel — Pavane pour une infante défunte
tracks.intro_text: From Maurice Ravel... the Pavane pour une infante défunte... Pavane for a Dead Princess. Ravel wrote it for piano in 1899, and later made a version for orchestra. Here is the original piano version, played by Thérèse Dussaut.

tracks.title: Saint-Saëns — The Swan
tracks.performer: Alisa Weilerstein, cello; Jason Yoder, piano
tracks.intro_text: From Camille Saint-Saëns... The Swan, from The Carnival of the Animals. Saint-Saëns wrote the suite in 1886 as a lighthearted entertainment, and The Swan was the only movement he allowed to be published in his lifetime. Cellist Alisa Weilerstein, with pianist Jason Yoder, recorded at the White House in 2009.

tracks.title: Bach — Brandenburg Concerto No. 3, I. Allegro
tracks.intro_text: From Johann Sebastian Bach... the first movement of the Brandenburg Concerto number 3 in G major, B.W.V. 1048, for three violins, three violas, three cellos, and continuo. Bach presented the six Brandenburg Concertos in 1721 to Christian Ludwig, Margrave of Brandenburg. Performed by the Advent Chamber Orchestra.

tracks.title: Bach — Brandenburg Concerto No. 3, III. Allegro
tracks.intro_text: Johann Sebastian Bach once more... the closing Allegro of the Brandenburg Concerto number 3 in G major, B.W.V. 1048... a brisk movement for strings alone. The Advent Chamber Orchestra.

tracks.title: Bach — Brandenburg Concerto No. 5, I. Allegro
tracks.intro_text: From Johann Sebastian Bach... the opening Allegro of the Brandenburg Concerto number 5 in D major, B.W.V. 1050, for flute, violin, and harpsichord, with strings. Near the end, the harpsichord breaks away in a long solo cadenza. The Advent Chamber Orchestra, with Roxana Pavel Goldstein, violin, Constance Schoepflin, flute, and Matthew Ganong, harpsichord.

tracks.title: Bach — Brandenburg Concerto No. 5, III. Allegro
tracks.intro_text: The finale now, of Bach's Brandenburg Concerto number 5 in D major, B.W.V. 1050... an Allegro in the spirit of a gigue. Roxana Pavel Goldstein, violin, Constance Schoepflin, flute, and Matthew Ganong, harpsichord, with the Advent Chamber Orchestra.

tracks.title: Bach — Brandenburg Concerto No. 6, III. Allegro
tracks.intro_text: From Johann Sebastian Bach... the final Allegro of the Brandenburg Concerto number 6 in B flat major, B.W.V. 1051... scored without violins, for the darker colors of violas, violas da gamba, and cello. Performed by the Advent Chamber Orchestra.

tracks.title: Bach — Keyboard Concerto in D minor, BWV 1052, I. Allegro
tracks.performer: Johannes Volker Schmidt, piano; Fulda Symphonic Orchestra
tracks.intro_text: Johann Sebastian Bach... the first movement, Allegro, of the Keyboard Concerto number 1 in D minor, B.W.V. 1052. Bach wrote his keyboard concertos in Leipzig, for the coffee-house concerts of the Collegium Musicum. Johannes Volker Schmidt is the piano soloist, with the Fulda Symphonic Orchestra, conducted by Simon Schindler.

tracks.title: Bach — Keyboard Concerto in D minor, BWV 1052, III. Allegro
tracks.performer: Johannes Volker Schmidt, piano; Fulda Symphonic Orchestra
tracks.intro_text: The finale of Bach's Keyboard Concerto number 1 in D minor, B.W.V. 1052... Allegro. Pianist Johannes Volker Schmidt, and the Fulda Symphonic Orchestra under Simon Schindler, recorded in the Prince's Hall of the City Palace in Fulda, Germany.

tracks.title: Bach — Concerto for Two Violins, BWV 1043, I. Vivace
tracks.performer: Advent Chamber Orchestra; David Parry & Roxana Pavel Goldstein
tracks.intro_text: From Johann Sebastian Bach... the Vivace, from the Concerto for Two Violins in D minor, B.W.V. 1043. The two solo parts weave around each other as equals, in close counterpoint. The soloists are David Parry and Roxana Pavel Goldstein, with the Advent Chamber Orchestra.

tracks.title: Bach — Concerto for Two Violins, BWV 1043, III. Allegro
tracks.performer: Advent Chamber Orchestra; David Parry & Roxana Pavel Goldstein
tracks.intro_text: The closing Allegro of Bach's Concerto for Two Violins in D minor, B.W.V. 1043... a work Bach later arranged as a concerto for two harpsichords. David Parry and Roxana Pavel Goldstein, violins, with the Advent Chamber Orchestra.

tracks.title: Bach — Preludio, Partita No. 3 in E, BWV 1006
tracks.intro_text: From Johann Sebastian Bach... the Preludio, from the Partita number 3 in E major for solo violin, B.W.V. 1006. Bach later reworked this music as the sinfonia of his cantata number 29. Tonight it is played on guitar, by Gordon Rowland.

tracks.title: Vivaldi — Spring, I. Allegro
tracks.intro_text: From Antonio Vivaldi... the opening Allegro of Spring, the Concerto in E major, opus 8, number 1, R.V. 269, from The Four Seasons. Vivaldi, the red-haired priest of Venice, matched each of the four concertos with a sonnet. The violinist is John Harrison, in a live performance.

tracks.title: Vivaldi — Summer, III. Presto
tracks.intro_text: Antonio Vivaldi... the Presto from Summer, the Concerto in G minor, opus 8, number 2, R.V. 315... a summer storm in music. John Harrison is the violin soloist, recorded live.

tracks.title: Vivaldi — Autumn, I. Allegro
tracks.intro_text: From The Four Seasons by Antonio Vivaldi... the first movement, Allegro, of Autumn, the Concerto in F major, opus 8, number 3, R.V. 293... a harvest celebration. Violinist John Harrison, in a live performance.

tracks.title: Vivaldi — Autumn, III. Allegro
tracks.intro_text: Vivaldi's Autumn, from The Four Seasons... the closing Allegro, the concerto in F major, R.V. 293, a picture of the hunt. Vivaldi spent much of his career teaching music at a Venetian home for orphaned girls. Played by violinist John Harrison.

tracks.title: Vivaldi — Winter, I. Allegro non molto
tracks.intro_text: From Antonio Vivaldi... the first movement, Allegro non molto, of Winter, the Concerto in F minor, opus 8, number 4, R.V. 297, from The Four Seasons, published in 1725. Violinist John Harrison, in a live performance.

tracks.title: Vivaldi — Winter, III. Allegro
tracks.intro_text: The finale of Vivaldi's Winter, from The Four Seasons... the Allegro of the Concerto in F minor, R.V. 297. Vivaldi published The Four Seasons in 1725, as the first four concertos of his opus 8. John Harrison, violin.

tracks.title: Handel — Alla Hornpipe, Water Music
tracks.intro_text: From George Frideric Handel... the Alla Hornpipe, from the Water Music, Suite number 2 in D major, H.W.V. 349. The Water Music was first played in 1717, on a barge on the River Thames, for King George the First. Performed by the Marine Chamber Orchestra of the United States Marine Band.

tracks.title: Handel — Arrival of the Queen of Sheba
tracks.intro_text: George Frideric Handel... the Arrival of the Queen of Sheba, the sinfonia that opens Act Three of his oratorio Solomon, from 1749. Handel was born in Germany, and spent most of his career in London. Performed by the Advent Chamber Orchestra.

tracks.title: Handel — Concerto Grosso in D minor, Op. 3 No. 5, HWV 316
tracks.performer: The London Baroque Orchestra, Alexander Hamilton (via Musopen)
tracks.intro_text: From George Frideric Handel... the Concerto Grosso in D minor, opus 3, number 5, H.W.V. 316. Handel's opus 3 concertos were published in London in 1734. The London Baroque Orchestra is directed by Alexander Hamilton.

tracks.title: Corelli — Concerto Grosso, Op. 6 No. 4, I
tracks.intro_text: From Arcangelo Corelli... the opening Adagio and Allegro, from the Concerto Grosso in D major, opus 6, number 4. Corelli was the great Italian violinist of his day, and his concerti grossi became models for Handel and many others. The Advent Chamber Orchestra.
